_doc: DUNHILL dating cabinet = DATA only, same general engine as Peterson. Now filled from the AUTHORITATIVE source Farid saved: the Pipedia Dunhill Dating Guide (based on Loring's & Field's guides) -> data/hub/pipes/brand_research/dunhill_dating/dunhill_dating_guide_FULL.txt, plus the local pipephil mirror. Proves the cabinet model generalises: Dunhill dates by date-code + finish + patent, a totally different system from Peterson, with NO engine change. Built + filled 2026-07-15.

brand_marks.physical: the inlaid WHITE SPOT on the top of the stem (from 1912) = Dunhill's own mark. A visual white-dot matcher can confirm brand later.
brand_marks.note: 'DUNHILL over DUKE ST S.W.' = 1910-1918; 'DUNHILL over LONDON' = Nov 1918-1952; from 1952 'DUNHILL over the FINISH NAME' (BRUYERE/ROOT BRIAR/etc).

finish_series._doc: Dunhill's finish IS the series, read VISUALLY (sandblast vs smooth) even if the word is worn. Gives a FLOOR (a pipe can't predate its finish) + the series label. Intros from the guide.

table.note: original smooth deep red-brown; Dunhill's first finish
iconic black sandblast; 'Shell' in quotes until 1934; possessive DUNHILL'S 'SHELL' 1918-1934
smooth light finish showing straight grain (guide: introduced 1931)
tan sandblast; the 'T' finish letter half-height from 1953
smooth mid-brown; intro approx -- verify in guide
deep rustication; intro approx -- verify in guide
straight-grain designation; pre-1931 on Bruyere ('DR'), post-1931 Root ('DRR')

patent_number._doc: Dunhill stamped patent numbers through 1954 (ceased 1955). A patent number present => PRE-1955. Specific numbers bracket the era. ENRICHED 2026-07-16 from the LOCAL pipephil mirror (logos/en/dunhill/patent1-3.html -- retro blog/platform sweep): usage eras below are pipephil's documented ones; where the Loring/Field guide disagrees the WIDE bracket is kept with a note.

table.note: Inner Tube patent (5681/12 = documented factory misstamp). Sources DISAGREE on end: pipephil 'used 1913-1926', guide table to 1935 -> wide kept
sandblast patent; the DOUBLE pattern '5861/12 119708/17' ('PATENT Nos') = 1918-1926 on Shells (pipephil)
US patent sometimes used in place of the primaries 1925-34 (pipephil)

the late patent, used 1942-1954 (pipephil patent3; guide sometimes shows it without /34 from 1935 -- if a bare '417574' turns up on a late-30s pipe widen honestly). Suffix on this patent is base-1940/1950 (guide: 1943='3', 1954='4') -> engine's candidate-intersection resolves or stays honestly ambiguous

date_code._doc: 'MADE IN ENGLAND n' suffix. REAL RULE (Pipedia guide, Loring/Field): from 1960 the suffix is a RUNNING number -> year = 1960 + n. England 4 = 1964, 15 = 1975, 24 = 1984, 44 = 2004, 64 = 2024. UNAMBIGUOUS -- no decade guess. 1955-59 used a single digit 5-9. PATENT-ERA RULE (guide + pipephil, added 2026-07-16): the suffix was INTRODUCED LATE 1921 and ran on RESTARTING bases while patents were stamped (to 1954): 1921-41 = 1920+n (documented: 5861/12+'3'=1923, '16'=1936, '21'=1941), 1940s = 1940+n (guide: 1943='3'), 1950-54 = 1950+n (guide: 1954='4' on 417574/34). Engine builds candidates from all bases and INTERSECTS with the matched patent's usage era -- one survivor = exact, else honest ambiguity. A patent pipe with NO suffix is pre-1921 (absence noted, never auto-dated).
